privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: ChatWizardBot is a Twitch chat bot, and this website is its companion statistics panel for the channels the bot serves. This page explains what data the service stores, why it stores it, and what you can do about it.
privacy.collectIntro: The bot joins only channels whose owners asked for it — it does not monitor Twitch at large. For those channels it stores:
privacy.collectChat: Public chat messages (text, Twitch username and user ID, channel, time) and statistics derived from them: message counts, word and emote frequencies, @mention counts.
privacy.collectMod: Moderation actions (bans, timeouts, deleted messages, warnings) with the acting moderator, the affected user and the time, plus moderator activity statistics.
privacy.collectNames: Username history — the usernames a Twitch account has previously used in tracked channels.
privacy.collectAccountIntro: If you log in to this site with your Twitch account, the site additionally stores:
privacy.collectAccount: Your Twitch ID, login, display name and avatar (received from Twitch when you log in), your login session, and your site preferences (language, profile privacy settings).
privacy.collectProfile: A cache of public Twitch profile data (avatar, chat color, display name) used to render pages; entries unused for 30 days are deleted automatically.
privacy.collectOwnerToken: If you own a connected channel: an encrypted copy of your Twitch refresh token, used in the background to keep that channel's moderator list synced with Twitch. It is deleted automatically if you revoke the site's access on Twitch, and you can ask us to delete it sooner (see "Your rights" below).
privacy.why1: The data exists solely to provide channel statistics: leaderboards, word and emote clouds, chat activity, and moderation analytics for channel owners and their moderators. Channels are added only at the owner's request, and the date of that request is recorded.
privacy.why2: Nothing is sold or shared with third parties. The site has no advertising and no third-party analytics.
privacy.cookies1: The site uses only technical cookies: a session cookie that keeps you logged in with Twitch and a cookie that remembers your language choice. There are no tracking or advertising cookies, which is why the site shows no cookie consent banner.
privacy.visibility1: Aggregated channel statistics (top chatters, word clouds, emote boards) are public.
privacy.visibility2: Raw chat logs and a channel's moderation history are visible only to that channel's owner and moderators.
privacy.visibility3: On your personal profile page, the message-volume chart and the activity calendar are hidden by default until you opt in; in your account settings you can also hide the entire profile from everyone — moderators included.
privacy.rights1: You can control what your profile page shows in your account settings at any time.
privacy.rightsContact: To ask what data is stored about you, or to request its correction or deletion, email
privacy.changes1: If this policy changes, the updated version will be published on this page with a new date.

useCase.counters: Check what counters exist before creating a duplicate.
useCase.counterUpdate: Viewers or mods bump a tally as events happen on stream.
useCase.addexception: Let a trusted regular update a mod-only counter without full mod status.
useCase.remexception: Revoke that trust if it's no longer needed.

durakMultiplayer.ruleAllowThrowInsDesc: Other players (not just the attacker) can toss in extra cards matching a rank already on the table. Turn off for classic single-card bouts.
durakMultiplayer.ruleAllowTransfersDesc: Instead of defending, a defender who holds a card of the same rank as the attack can lay it down and pass the whole undefended pile to the next player, who becomes the new defender.
durakMultiplayer.ruleDeckSizeDesc: 36 cards (ranks 6-14) is the classic deck. 52 cards (ranks 2-14, no jokers) is a common house rule for large tables. At exactly 6 players, 36 cards deals every player's whole hand with nothing left in reserve - no draws, and the trump card stays visible for the whole game instead of sitting in a reserve pile.

sunduchki.mpRule1: On your turn, pick a player and a rank you already hold at least one card of — no bluffing on the rank. If they hold none at all, your turn ends right there
sunduchki.mpRule2: If they do hold some, you must then guess exactly how many and name every one of those suits to take the cards — get the count or any suit wrong and it's a miss, but a full hit gets you all of them at once and you go again
sunduchki.mpRule3: If you miss, you draw a card from the deck and the turn passes to the next player
sunduchki.mpRule4: Collect all 4 cards of a rank to lay down a chest, shown to everyone right away
sunduchki.mpRule5: Every question and answer is public — listen closely to figure out who holds what
sunduchki.mpRule6: Up to 6 players at one table; the host chooses the deck size and whether you can ask anyone or only the next player
sunduchki.mpRule7: Ratings use an Elo system - beating a stronger opponent earns more than beating a weaker one, and losing to a weaker opponent costs more than losing to a stronger one. Your rating appears after your first finished game
sunduchki.mpRule8: Each player gets a 5-minute clock for the whole game, chess-clock style — it only runs on your turn. Run it out and you're out
sunduchki.mpRule9: Starting a game opens a 45s ready check - everyone (host included) must click Accept, or they're dropped from the room

channelSettings.bannedWordsIntro: A user is timed out if they type one of these words and ping the bot with "@ChatWizardBot" in the same message.

channelSettings.spamSignaturesIntro: A message is re-obfuscated (homoglyphs, spacing tricks, etc. normalized back to plain text) before being checked against these signatures. Each signature can have its own ban duration (up to permanent) and its own reason.
channelSettings.spamSignaturesExample: Example signature "subscribe to my channel ExampleChannel" also catches messages using modified/obfuscated fonts to spell it out.

channelSettings.detectionToggleHint: When on, the bot times out users who type a banned word while pinging it.
channelSettings.sevenTvNotLinked: No 7TV account found for this channel
channelSettings.unbanBureauIntro: Turns on the appeal review desk for this channel and the advisory chat vote you can start from it. While off, the bot doesn't poll Twitch for this channel's appeals at all.
channelSettings.unbanBureauEnabledHint: Mirrors this channel's unban appeals so they can be reviewed on the site.
channelSettings.unbanBureauVoteHint: A vote opens by itself when an appeal reaches the window and closes when you stamp a verdict — there is no timer. Chat votes with these two Twitch emotes and the bot stays silent about it; the result is advisory.
channelSettings.unbanBureauSniperHint: The rifle on the wall by the desk: a moderator fires it by hand and the bot punishes one random chatter. The bot never fires by itself — not on a vote, not on a verdict. Moderators, the broadcaster and bot accounts are never hit, and the target is picked server-side rather than by the page. The more recent someone's message, the likelier they are to be hit: whoever just typed is about 16 times likelier than someone whose message is about to fall out of the two-minute window. Below is what happens to whoever it hits.
channelSettings.unbanBureauGrenadeHint: The desk's second weapon. The grenade takes everyone who spoke in chat in the last 30 seconds instead of one viewer. Same exclusions as the rifle: moderators, the broadcaster and bot accounts are never caught in the blast. One throw hits at most 20 people — in a live chat an unlimited radius stops being a joke and becomes a mass ban issued by one click. It cannot be spammed: after a throw it is unavailable to the whole channel at once, however many moderators are at the desk, and the reload cannot be set shorter than 5 minutes.
channelSettings.autoBehaviorIntro: Features the bot performs on its own, without a chat command — each can be turned on or off individually.

requestBot.title: Request the bot
requestBot.subtitle: Ask for ChatWizardBot to be added to your Twitch channel.
requestBot.connectedNotice: Your channel is already connected to the bot.
requestBot.pendingBody: An administrator will review it soon. Once approved, the bot joins your channel after its next restart.
requestBot.modNoticeBody: The bot needs moderator rights on your channel to work properly (timeouts, spam protection, deleting messages). Type this in your channel's chat:
requestBot.rejectedRetryHint: You can submit a new request below.
requestBot.messageHint: Anything the administrator should know about your channel.
requestBot.modAckLabel: I have granted (or will grant) the bot moderator rights on my channel

errors.mod_ack_required: Please confirm the moderator-rights checkbox first.

ai.memoryPageHint: Facts about the channel the bot wrote down for itself while answering, plus the ones added here by hand. Not the whole list goes into a call - only the facts whose words match the question; hand-written ones always go.
ai.memoryWritesOff: Self-remembering is switched off in the settings: the bot still reads this list but adds nothing new.
ai.memoryRecallHint: Sent with one call (plus hand-written ones):
ai.addFactPlaceholder: For example: the stream usually starts at 19:00
ai.memoryEmpty: The bot has not remembered anything about this channel yet.
ai.memoryChannelAiOff: AI replies are off for this channel - the bot answers nothing here, so there is nothing for it to remember. Turn them on under the Channels tab.

factEditError.duplicate: That fact is already stored - the edit was cancelled rather than making two identical rows.
factEditError.empty: An empty fact cannot be saved. Use Delete to remove it.
factEditError.failed: The edit could not be saved.
factEditError.unknownUser: The bot has never seen this viewer in this chat, so there is nobody to file the fact against. Use the login they chatted under.

ai.channelMemoryEnabled: The bot remembers on its own
ai.channelMemoryEnabledHint: Let the bot add facts about the channel to its memory while it answers. Switching this off erases nothing: the list is still read, it just stops growing.
ai.channelMemoryMaxHint: How many facts the bot keeps for a channel. Counts its own rows only - hand-written ones are neither counted nor evicted. Not a spend setting: only the facts picked out for the question are sent. Over the ceiling the bot's least recently used rows go first. Zero means the bot never remembers.
ai.channelMemoryRecallHint: How many question-matching facts ride along with one billed call - this is the spend. Hand-written facts go on top of this number: they are always sent.
ai.channelMemoryLink: See what the bot has remembered
ai.reviewChange: Press the other button to change this mark
ai.keyMissing: The site has no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Chat replies need the key on the BOT, not the site - check TwitchBot/.env.
ai.limitReached: Daily limit reached. Until midnight the bot falls back to its scripted replies.
ai.masterSwitchHint: The master switch. Off stops replies on every channel at once. The bot only answers while the channel is live: off air a mention falls through to the scripted replies, exactly as it does with the feature switched off.
ai.modelHint: Each provider has its own key in the bot's .env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for claude-*, GEMINI_API_KEY for gemini-*. Without the right key the bot falls back to its scripted replies and says nothing about it. gemini-3.5-flash-lite has a free tier - it is bounded by request count rather than money (limits live in AI Studio), and Google trains on what is sent: viewer messages and the memory about them.
ai.dailyLimitHint: Shared across all channels. Cache and filter hits do not count - they never reach the model.
ai.cooldownHint: Minimum gap between two AI replies in one chat.
ai.requestTimeoutHint: How long to wait for the model. An answer arriving more than 10 seconds after the question is dropped entirely.
ai.memoryPairsHint: How many past exchanges with the same viewer the model sees.
ai.memoryTtlHint: The journal is also the memory: older rows expire automatically.
ai.punishHint: The model may propose a timeout for outright nonsense. In observe mode the proposal is only written to the journal.
ai.systemPromptHint: The whole rule text sent to the model before every call. The field holds what is in effect right now - edit it like ordinary text. The persona below is appended as a separate paragraph.
ai.systemPromptWarning: Careful: the memory blocks here are what makes the bot remember at all. Drop the channel-memory block (remember/forget) and it stops recording facts about the channel; drop the viewer-memory block (rememberAbout) and everything it learns about people goes into the channel memory instead. Neither raises an error. The hard bans (links, "@", a leading "!", length) are enforced by the sanitizer after the model and editing this text does not lift them.
ai.systemPromptBuiltinInUse: The bot's built-in rules are in effect. Editing here replaces them with yours.
ai.systemPromptCustom: Your own rules are in effect - built-in updates do not reach the bot, including blocks added after you saved your text. To go back to the built-in rules, press the button below the field and save.
ai.systemPromptBuiltinUnknown: The built-in text is not known yet - the bot writes it on its next start.
ai.personaHint: The part of the prompt shared by every channel: who the bot is and how it talks. The rules and prohibitions live in code and this field does not override them.
ai.channelsHint: AI is enabled per channel. A new channel starts switched off.
ai.aiEnabledHint: The channel owner neither sees nor changes this.
ai.toneHint: How the bot talks here specifically. Added on top of the shared persona.
ai.cheatsheetHint: What the bot should know: who streams, what they play, in-jokes. Anything not here, the model does not know and must say so.
ai.cooldownsHint: Numbers that used to live on the channel settings page. The word and phrase lists stayed with the owner.
ai.insultCumulativeHint: A repeat offence inside this window lengthens the timeout.
ai.filterHint: Messages not worth spending a request on. Matching is exact, so "hi" and "hi!" are two different entries. Entries are per channel: the model writes them itself, and a shared table would serve an answer it invented in one chat to every other one. Text and answer can be corrected in place.

filterEditError.duplicate: An entry with that text already exists - the edit was cancelled rather than silently dropping one of the two answers.
filterEditError.empty: Neither the text nor the answer can be empty: the bot serves a filter entry without asking the model, so a blank one counts a hit and then falls through to the model anyway. Use Delete to remove the entry.
filterEditError.failed: The edit could not be saved - there is no longer an entry with that text.

ai.filterEmpty: The filter is empty so far.
ai.cacheHint: Ready answers the model marked as durable. The cache is per channel: the same question has different right answers in different chats.

cacheFate.volatile: not cached: tied to the moment

ai.verdictsHint: What the model proposed to punish. Mark agree/disagree - it is the only basis for switching to enforce.
ai.verdictsEmpty: The model has not proposed a punishment yet.
ai.ignoredHint: Viewers the bot no longer answers with AI. The mark is permanent and can only be lifted here.
ai.viewersPageHint: What the bot knows about individual viewers: facts it wrote while answering, plus anything added here by hand. Only the memory of the people in the exchange is sent with a question - the asker, and anyone they named.
ai.viewerMemoryWritesOff: Learning about viewers is switched off in the settings: the bot still reads these lists but adds nothing new.
ai.viewerMemoryEmpty: The bot has not learnt anything about this channel's viewers yet.
ai.userMemoryEnabledHint: Let the bot write down facts about people in chat. A viewer can tell it about themselves, or anyone else in the same exchange can - who said it is always shown on the row. Switching this off keeps what is stored: the lists are still read.
ai.userMemoryMaxHint: How many facts the bot holds about one person. Here that number IS the spend: only the memory of people in the exchange is sent, so no second number is needed as it is for the channel. Counts the bot's own rows only - hand-written ones are never evicted. On overflow, facts from less authoritative authors go first, and among equals the least recently used. Zero means the bot learns nothing about viewers.
ai.userMemoryLink: See what the bot has learnt about viewers
ai.viewerFilterEmpty: No such login in the list.

admin.title: Admin panel
admin.subtitle: Bot-join requests, channels, and service health.
admin.diskUsageIntro: Hourly samples of MongoDB's own storage stats, written by the bot - which collections are actually growing, and how fast the disk is filling up.
admin.diskUsageEmpty: Not enough samples yet - the bot writes one every hour, come back once a few have landed.
admin.diskUsageCollectionsIntro: Sorted fastest-growing first - a collection whose growth is negative or zero shrank or held steady over the sample window.
admin.memoryIntro: Machine memory as the bot sees it, sampled every 30s and stored as hourly min/avg/max. The minimum is the number that matters: it is how close the machine came to running out.
admin.memoryEmpty: No samples yet - the bot writes a bucket per hour, come back once one has landed.
admin.memoryNoSwapBody: With no swap the kernel cannot page anything out under pressure - it terminates a process instead (OOM killer). That looks like a sudden restart with nothing in the log, so the floor below has to stay clear of zero.
admin.memorySwapUnknown: Swap state unknown (no /proc on this host)
admin.memoryChartLegend: Line = hourly average, band = hourly min/max spread.
admin.memoryBotIntro: This process only. A machine-wide fall with a flat line here is somebody else's memory - mongod or the web panel.
admin.memoryProcessesIntro: Latest snapshot, everything above 20 MB. Read from procfs, so nothing is shown on a non-Linux host.
admin.visitsIntro: Page views per day for the last 30 days (excludes static files and pages' own background JSON polling).
admin.gamesIntro: Completed sessions/matches per game, plus how many distinct players have saved a score or rating - ranked by sessions. Vs-computer Durak is never counted here - its results never leave the browser.

games.visibilityHint: Hidden games disappear from the public /games hub immediately - their own page and score submission keep working for anyone with the direct link.
games.categoriesHint: Group games into sections on the /games hub, e.g. "Interesting games" / "Boring games". A game with no category falls into the unlabeled section at the end. Each category needs a name in every supported language, so it always reads correctly for visitors on either locale.
games.categoriesEmpty: No categories yet - the hub shows a flat list until you add one.

flash.categoryDeleted: Category deleted. Games in it are now uncategorized.

flash.approved: Request approved and channel registered. The bot joins the channel within a minute.
flash.enabled: Channel enabled. The bot joins it within a minute.
flash.disabled: Channel disabled. The bot leaves it at its next restart.
flash.homepageShown: Channel is now shown on the home page.
flash.homepageHidden: Channel hidden from the home page.
flash.newsEnabled: News feed enabled for the channel.
flash.newsDisabled: News feed disabled for the channel.
flash.deleted: The entire settings change log has been deleted.

admin.healthNoTokenHint: Scheduled moderator sync is off for these channels until their owner logs in to the site:
admin.botNoData: No heartbeat recorded yet - the bot hasn't reported in since this feature was deployed, or it's down.
admin.botEventsHint: Red is a failure that did not recover on its own; green is one the bot fixed itself. Identical lines collapse into one with a counter.
admin.botDegradedPending: {{label}} - failed {{since}} ago, waiting for it to recover ({{detail}})
admin.gqlPausedHint: The token is fine - it is the requests that are paused, because Twitch refused them or did not answer. Last failure {{failedAgo}}, {{failures}} in a row, reason: "{{reason}}". While paused the Amnesty Bureau shows the bot's own log counts instead of Twitch's. Nothing to do; retrying {{retryIn}}.
admin.gqlTokenExpiredHint: Twitch rejected the private-GraphQL session token (gql_auth_token) {{failedAgo}}, so the Amnesty Bureau's moderator comments and real ban/timeout counts are unavailable. Re-capture the auth-token cookie of a logged-in moderator session into the bot's .env. Retrying automatically {{retryIn}}.
admin.requestsApproveHint: Approving registers the channel; the bot joins it after its next restart.
admin.channelsHint: Disabling removes the channel from the site's home page and from the bot's join list at its next restart. "On home page" separately hides a channel from the home page only - the site and bot keep working with it as normal.

news.formError: Please fill in every field - a title, body text, and (for a new post) a hero image.
news.formHint: Posts are published immediately and appear at the top of the channel's news feed.
news.noEnabledChannels: No channel has the news feed enabled yet - turn it on from the Overview tab first.
news.currentImageHint: Current image - upload a new one to replace it.
news.formatHint: Markdown is rendered to HTML; HTML is used as-is. Both are sanitized before publishing.

pageThemes.title: User page themes
pageThemes.hint: A theme replaces the default look of /<channel>/user/<name>. It belongs to the user, not the channel, so it applies on their page in every channel.
pageThemes.editHint: These settings apply to this user's page in every channel.
pageThemes.accentHint: The palette sets the whole room - background, text, gilding and chart colours; each skin has its own set. A custom colour only changes the gilding in the header - frames, highlights and the throne's outlines - and never the background or the text, so the page stays readable.
pageThemes.backdropScopeHint: Whole page pins the columns and wallpaper to the window, so the page scrolls inside the hall; the cornice stays above the throne either way.
pageThemes.medallionHint: Left empty, the medallion shows the Twitch avatar.
pageThemes.steamHint: A Steam profile URL. Items are read from that profile's Item Showcase when the URL changes or when the box below is ticked; the profile must be public. Clearing the field removes the case.
pageThemes.steamError: Could not read the Steam showcase: the profile is private, unreachable, or has no Item Showcase. The previous case has been kept.
pageThemes.fieldIntro: Play the cloud intro on arrival
pageThemes.trophiesHint: Left to right. Repeats are replaced with the defaults.
pageThemes.deleteConfirm: Delete this theme and its uploaded files?
pageThemes.uploadError: File rejected: too large, or not an image.
pageThemes.imageError: That image could not be processed.
pageThemes.quotaError: This user's file storage limit would be exceeded.

error.unknownUser: No such user in the chat chronicle.

admin.gameRunsIntro: Solo-game runs the anti-cheat wants a human to look at. Their scores are held off the leaderboard until you approve them - the run itself is kept intact either way.
admin.gameRunsApproveConfirm: Publish this run's score to the leaderboard?
admin.gameRunsResetConfirm: Reject this run and delete this player's stored best score for this game? This cannot be undone.

gameRunsReason.scoreMismatch: Claimed more than the replay scored
gameRunsReason.scoreOverrun: Replay scored more than claimed (likely our bug)
gameRunsReason.timeTravel: Run simulated longer than it actually lasted
gameRunsReason.wrongGame: Log was for a different game
gameRunsReason.replayTruncated: Run outran the replay's step limit
gameRunsReason.checkpointGap: Mid-run checkpoint is missing part of the log
gameRunsReason.impossibleRate: Scored faster than the game allows
gameRunsReason.impossiblePerEvent: Scored more than the inputs allow
gameRunsReason.impossibleClimb: Climbed faster than the game allows
gameRunsReason.legacyCapExceeded: Untokened score above the plausible cap
gameRunsReason.ceilingDisagreesWithReplay: Rate ceiling disagrees with the replay
gameRunsReason.beaconOversize: Log too large to send on leaving
gameRunsReason.lowJitter: Input timing too consistent for a hand
gameRunsReason.superhumanApm: More actions per second than a human sustains

unbanBureau.title: Amnesty Bureau
unbanBureau.subtitle: Review unban appeals
unbanBureau.shiftBusyBody: One of your colleagues is working the desk right now. Wait until their shift is over.
unbanBureau.shiftBusyJustStarted: The shift has only just started.
unbanBureau.shiftTakeOverNote: The moderator loses their shift and is told so. Use this when a tab was left open and abandoned.
unbanBureau.shiftLostBody: Your shift ended and another moderator has taken the desk. They are handling the queue now.
unbanBureau.allDone: Every appeal in the queue has been dealt with.
unbanBureau.disabled: The Amnesty Bureau is off for this channel. Turn it on in settings to start mirroring appeals.
unbanBureau.humansOnlyNote: Counts exclude actions taken by bot accounts.
unbanBureau.resolutionPlaceholder: Shown to them on Twitch, up to 500 characters
unbanBureau.shortcutHint: A — approve · D — deny · → — next case
unbanBureau.queued: Decision recorded — the bot will apply it on Twitch within a minute.
unbanBureau.approveScheduled: Approval recorded — the bot will unban them on {{date}}.
unbanBureau.decisionFailed: Twitch refused the decision — the appeal may already be closed. Try again.
unbanBureau.voteAdvisory: Advisory only — the decision stays yours.
unbanBureau.voteQueued: The bot will post the vote in chat shortly.
unbanBureau.sniperMissed: The Bureau aimed at {{target}} and missed.
unbanBureau.alreadyDecided: This appeal has already been decided.
unbanBureau.voteAlreadyRunning: A vote is already running on this appeal.
unbanBureau.commentsEmpty: No moderator has left a comment about this user.
unbanBureau.actionsEmpty: No punishments on record for this user.
unbanBureau.contextHint: hover for the messages sent before this
unbanBureau.contextEmpty: No messages from before this action were kept.
unbanBureau.countsFromTwitch: From Twitch: this channel's lifetime totals.
unbanBureau.countsFromBot: Only since the bot joined — Twitch is unavailable, the real numbers may be higher.
unbanBureau.sharingOff: This channel does not take part in Twitch ban sharing — comments and bans from other channels are not visible here.
unbanBureau.expertsEmpty: No opinions were written on this case.
unbanBureau.expertsGenerated: The hearing is ready — come back to this case.
unbanBureau.expertsGenerateFailed: Could not compose the hearing. Try again.
unbanBureau.expertsGenerateUnavailable: Hearing generation is not configured on this server.
unbanBureau.expertsGenerateTooMany: Too many hearings in a row. Try again later.
unbanBureau.expertRewritten: The charge above was rewritten after hearing the defence.
unbanBureau.rulesEmpty: This channel has no posted chat rules (or the bot hasn't fetched them from Twitch yet).
unbanBureau.needStamp: Stamp the visa before handing it back.
unbanBureau.sniperQueued: Shot fired — the bot is picking a target.
unbanBureau.sniperNoTarget: Nobody in chat to hit right now.
unbanBureau.sniperRejected: Twitch refused the punishment — the shot missed.
unbanBureau.grenadeArmed: Grenade in hand. Right-click to put it away.
unbanBureau.grenadeQueued: Thrown — the bot is rounding up everyone who spoke in the last 30 seconds.
unbanBureau.grenadeNoTarget: Chat has been silent for 30 seconds — the grenade hit nobody.
unbanBureau.grenadeRejected: Twitch refused to punish anyone in the blast.
